client.name: Archipelago's SNI Client
client._source: SCHEMA rule 1, read from the world itself: Silvris/Archipelago (branch kss) worlds/kss/client.py, 2026-08-23 -- `class KSSSNIClient(SNIClient)`. The guide agrees, describing SNIClient launching automatically. ⚠ Recording the world's OWN transport. London does not run upstream's client -- see catalog/games/smw.json, where an SNIClient world is driven by a BizHawk RAM map instead and the protocol was set to bizhawk for that reason. Whoever writes this game's RAM map must set the protocol to match the bridge the map actually targets. ⚠ Rule 2 is NOT satisfied either: no RAM map Plugins/Scripts/games/kirby_super_star.lua exists, so the build refuses this manifest.

apworld._source: catalog/sheet_links.json, the "APWorld, Poptracker" link for Kirby Super Star. The setup guide names no source.

patch._source: world source: worlds/kss/rom.py, read 2026-08-23 -- `class KSSProcedurePatch(APProcedurePatch, APTokenMixin)` with `patch_file_ending = ".apkss"`. The guide agrees: "Your patch file should have a `.apkss` extension."

_patch_extension_source: world source: worlds/kss/rom.py, read 2026-08-23 -- the world defines `KSSPatchExtensions` with TWO methods: `apply_basepatch` and `apply_bsdiff4`. ⚠⚠ READ THIS BEFORE RECLASSIFYING. `apply_basepatch` is a NEW step name, which London's patcher refuses loudly -- that is why this field says "refused". But `apply_bsdiff4` is a GENERIC step name the launcher already implements, REDEFINED by this world. That is the FRLG class: generic code would run its own apply_bsdiff4, the checksum guard would pass, and the ROM would be silently wrong. This must NOT be moved to "none", and may only become "replicated" once the world's apply_bsdiff4 is replicated in Core/Patching/ApPatch.cs with the source cited.
